stem: A team wants to move suspect material into an unaffected lot to free rack space. What is the problem?
choices: Moving suspect material into an unaffected lot can destroy segregation, blur lot identity, and contaminate the evidence needed to support disposition.
The move is acceptable if both lots remain in the same room and are labeled separately afterward.
The move is acceptable if the suspect material appears normal because the hold is precautionary rather than confirmed.
The move improves traceability because comparing suspect and unaffected material in one rack simplifies observation.
rationale: Segregation protects both product control and evidence integrity. Mixing suspect material with unaffected product can create cross-contact, confuse genealogy, and make it harder to determine which material experienced the original condition. Rack-space pressure does not justify weakening the hold; any movement should preserve identity and follow the authorized containment/disposition process.
